metadata.title: An exact period criterion for focal-distance products in elliptic billiards
metadata.description:
For a noncircular elliptic billiard with a strictly nested nondegenerate confocal elliptical caustic, the product of ordinary distances from all vertices to either fixed focus is independent of phase if and only if the primitive least period is congruent to 2 modulo 4. The result covers all admissible primitive star turns and both orientations. For every even least period, the two focal products are equal at each phase. Repetitions raise the positive primitive product to an integer power, so listed return length alone is insufficient. Circles are treated separately; hyperbolic and degenerate caustics are excluded.

This research note proves the primitive interpretation of the experimentally recorded invariant k114 in Reznik–Garcia–Koiller (2020/2021), establishes the exact period classification, and gives an exact doubled-triangle counterexample to the unrestricted six-event return interpretation. It applies Stachel's published parametrization, classical Jacobi identities and established meromorphic divisor methods. No new-method or exclusive historical priority claim is made. The bounded primary-source audit found no explicit earlier proof of this exact target; novelty of the specific formulation is not certified. Full text of one related 2023 Dragović–Gajić article was unavailable, and the accompanying priority note records that coverage gap.

The deposit contains the manuscript PDF and a support archive with standalone LaTeX source, exact finite arithmetic controls, independent supplementary theta-series diagnostics, recorded outputs, metadata, references and priority-search limits. Finite checks support the analytic all-period proof; floating-point computations are not validated numerical certification.

metadata.title: A cone-angle proof of Fuchs's labelled length-ratio conjecture
metadata.description:
This research note gives a cone-angle and classical Veech-cusp proof of Fuchs's Conjecture 2.7: the lengths of source-parallel first-vertex billiard trajectories in every regular n-gon, n≥3, have the canonical labelled sine ratio. The proof includes sides, odd and even double polygons, the physical folding-chart sign, segment-parity reversal, and separate triangular, square and hexagonal marked-lattice cases.

Alper Ferudun's unrefereed preprint of 9 October 2026, DOI10.5281/zenodo.23267641, already states and proves the same nontrivial all-n theorem by angular indices, explicit uniform twists and descent. This note presents a different proof, credits that exact overlapping solution and classical cone-angle/hyperelliptic/Veech machinery, and claims neither a new invariant nor first or exclusive resolution. The repository candidate of 30 September 2026 predates that release, but its substantive folding-chart and physical-reversal correction was recorded on 11 October 2026 at23:57UTC and accepted on 12 October 2026 UTC. We describe the two proof routes as contemporaneous separate developments. The dates do not certify either author's awareness of the other's work or a literally simultaneous publication instant. The corrected proof is not backdated; historical novelty and first or exclusive priority are not certified.

metadata.title: A counterexample to ideal closure of property-(s) elements in skew braces
metadata.description:
This concise research note gives an explicit counterexample to Colazzo's unrestricted question asking whether the elements with property (s) in a skew left brace form an ideal. On the abelian additive group Z x Z/4Z, a standard semidirect multiplication gives exactly S = Z x {0,1}. The element (0,1) has both defining indices equal to two; its additive double has both indices infinite. The proof is self-contained over all integers and also shows failure of lambda-invariance.

The finite brace, semidirect construction and high-bit action have established antecedents in Bachiller, Smoktunowicz-Vendramin and Dietzel. Prior finite-conjugacy characterizations and simple infinite-module variations of Di Matteo-Ferrara and Mondal-Shumyatsky-Trombetti-Yadav are credited. Alper Ferudun's unrefereed October 11, 2026 preprint, DOI10.5281/zenodo.23292254, gives exactly the same counterexample. GitHub records our original PR156 on September 30, 2026 at12:24:37UTC; its mathematical proof is unchanged. This formal preprint is not backdated. We describe these as contemporaneous separate discoveries, meaning separate disclosures in the same period. Mutual independence, literally simultaneous release, historical novelty, first and exclusive priority are not certified. The bounded priority audit found no earlier explicit negative answer in the complete bodies read, but several publisher bodies were unavailable; the exact gaps and available versions are recorded.

metadata.title: A regular zero-area singularity with a nonzero weak Bianchi defect
metadata.description:
We give a counterexample to the geometric regular-zero-area-singularity implication in the Oberwolfach report conjecture (problem 30004807 / OWR-8415343-010), under the cited Burtscher-Kiessling-Tahvildar-Zadeh convention of smooth compactly supported vector fields reaching the retained inner boundary and regularity of the static spacelike slices. The spacetime is a negative-mass specialization of the known Dadhich-Kar-Mukherjee-Visser metric, whose tensor formulas are credited. Its static slices have harmonically regular zero-area singularities of mass -2a. We prove absolute convergence of the complete weak Bianchi scalar for every permitted test and compute an explicit nonzero boundary functional, with value -8 pi for a normalized radial test. The boundary-flux method is credited to the existing literature; convergence is established directly, without invoking a sufficient theorem outside its hypotheses.

The example violates the null energy condition. Added energy conditions, prescribed matter models, arbitrary tilted-slice regularity, collapsed-point test fields and the wider matter/evolution program are outside the claim. No new metric, new tensor formula, new general boundary theorem, historical first priority or continued-openness certificate is claimed. The priority search is extensive but bounded.

metadata.title: Loss of total-space positivity for the normalized relative Kähler–Ricci flow
metadata.description:
We give a negative answer to the total-space positivity-preservation question for the probability-normalized relative Kähler–Ricci flow defined by Naumann on O_E(r). For E = O(1) ⊕ O(1) over the projective line, a smooth strictly positive initial metric on O_E(2) = O(2,2) evolves to horizontal curvature exactly −1/96 at time (log 2)/2. The four-page research note proves global initial positivity and derives the exact second-variation evolution along a stationary central fiber.

The flow construction was already known; the result addresses the explicit positivity question in the original report and published article, rather than the Griffiths conjecture or other normalizations. The deposit includes manuscript source, reproducible exact verification, independent mathematical audits, and a bounded primary-source priority audit. Historical first priority is not asserted; a relevant 2025 Naumann habilitation was identified but its text was not recovered. Smooth finite-time flow existence is a cited analytic input, not a computational conclusion.

metadata.title: NP-completeness of three-terminal shortest-path blocking
metadata.description:
We prove NP-completeness of undirected, unit-traversal-length three-terminal Blocking Shortest Paths: delete a minimum edge set to increase every pairwise terminal distance by at least one. Hardness holds with unit deletion costs and all three original terminal distances equal to three. A direct Vertex Cover reduction also proves NP-completeness when all terminal distances must remain finite, or increase exactly from three to four. The result classifies the undirected triangle question posed by Stefan Krause in 2005. The classical subdivision identity is credited to Poljak (1974), and the related tripartite attachment mechanism to Khachiyan and coauthors (2008). Historical first priority and continued open status through 2026 are not asserted.

This unrefereed research note includes a source and verification archive with the unchanged original proof packet, explicit hash manifests, source-free standard-library Python reproduction, independent adversarial mathematical and computational audits, source-model checks and a bounded priority audit. metadata.title: The outer-pedal area centroid in even-period elliptic billiards
metadata.description: We prove the k307 outer-side pedal area-centroid observation of Reznik, Garcia and Koiller for billiards in a noncircular ellipse with a strict confocal elliptic caustic and least even period. The ordered perpendicular feet of any fixed point on the boundary tangent lines have an explicit phase-independent signed area centroid wherever their signed area is nonzero. We classify the entire zero-area locus: none when d is nonnegative, and a fixed circle when d is negative. Simple winding-one even families have a centroid for every fixed point; the four-period value is M/3. An exact primitive eight-period star shows that the exceptional undefined locus is real. The note supplies an all-period support-coordinate and cubic-moment proof. The verification archive contains the LaTeX source, exact symbolic and rational certificates, independent high-precision orbit controls, audit reports and reproducibility instructions. metadata.title: Full stress stratifications determine a labelled graph
metadata.description:
For every positive n and d, a simple graph on a fixed labelled vertex set is determined by its full connected coordinate-sign self-stress partition of (R^d)^n, with all vertex collisions retained. An unordered pair is an edge exactly when its collision diagonal is a union of whole strata. Thus two such partitions are literally equal precisely when their edge sets agree. This gives a complete answer to the literal equality interpretation of Problem 4 in Karpenkov (2018), DOI 10.1007/s40598-018-0080-7.

The proof combines Panina's known collapsed-edge criterion with elementary positive diagonal transport along a connected collinear path. No novelty is claimed for the detector, stress equivalence machinery, collinear invariance or incidence normalization. Arbitrary ambient or abstract equivalence, generic-only or collision-free comparisons, and pure-condition comparisons are different questions. The note exhibits nonisomorphic trees with ambient-linearly equivalent full stratifications.

The deposit includes a concise proof, TeX source, a source/priority supplement, independent adversarial review records, and exact-rational verification with three independent checkers and actual defective-source mutation controls (Python 3.10 or later on POSIX, such as macOS or Linux). Finite diagnostics support formulas and boundary cases; the written proof supplies universal and connectedness claims. A bounded priority search located no earlier exact reconstruction theorem in inspected sources, without certifying exhaustive originality or unwritten author intent. metadata.title: A Martin kernel with isolated Harnack contact in an annulus
metadata.description:
For the annulus 1 < |z| < e, with base point a = exp(1/2), the normalized minimal Martin kernel at the inner-boundary point -1 is strictly below the envelope of normalized positive harmonic functions throughout a punctured neighborhood of a. Four explicit positive harmonic competitors yield a uniform first-order gap in every direction. Direct Green-kernel construction and harmonic reflection establish the Martin limit and minimality.

This gives a negative answer to the equality-along-a-Green-line extension in Hayman and Lingham, Research Problems in Function Theory, arXiv:1809.07200v2, Problem 7.42, attributed to Arsove and Johnson. The statement concerns equality along a line issuing from the base point; it does not exclude isolated contact farther away. A dated, bounded priority audit accompanies the authored verification package. An addendum proves that a simpler punctured-disc counterexample is an elementary deduction from classical positive-harmonic representations, including Kohn (1966); this does not establish prior recognition of the Green-line consequence or yield the smooth-annulus theorem. No claim of first historical resolution or certification of current worldwide openness is made.

The deposit contains a concise research note and authored proof source, independent adversarial reviews and reproducibility materials. OpenAI tools were used extensively in solving, drafting and verifying the result. This is an unrefereed preprint, with no completed human peer review or formal proof-assistant certification claimed. Integrity checks and numerical checks do not replace the analytic proof.

metadata.title: A characteristic-two counterexample to dévissage for local deformation functors
metadata.description:

metadata.title: An odd-period pedal-antipedal area invariant in elliptic billiards
metadata.description: We prove the k403,a observation of Reznik, Garcia and Koiller: the signed area product of the original orbit's origin pedal and origin antipedal is phase independent for every primitive least odd period in a noncircular elliptic billiard with a strict confocal elliptical caustic. metadata.title: An application of separable-state nonrepresentability to Grassmann orbitopes and calibrations
metadata.description:
An application of Fawzi's established finite semidefinite lift obstruction for normalized complex separable states to the oriented real Grassmann orbitope C(4,12), the mass ball in the fourth exterior power of real 12-space. Two affine hyperplanes select a section real-linearly isomorphic to Sep(3,3). This mass ball has no finite projected semidefinite lift of any size. A compact first-moment argument refutes the universal degree-at-most-one supporting sum-of-squares assertion in Sanyal's Oberwolfach Report 13/2015, pp. 708–709, in joint work with Rostalski. It gives a negative answer in general to Harvey–Lawson Question 6.5: some constant closed comass-one four-form has no pointwise or local norm completion.

The conclusion is existential. A failing unnormalized functional with rational coefficients exists, but no explicit coefficient list, exact comass, rational normalized calibration, least dimension or low-dimensional classification is supplied. Classical Wirtinger and Kähler faces, established fermionic projector bodies, Vrana–Lévay's tensor-to-wedge decomposability lemma, theta-body and lift frameworks, and the earlier Sanyal–Rostalski equivalence are credited. Fawzi supplies the decisive no-lift theorem, public in 2019 and published in 2021; it is not reproved. Nearby quadratic Grassmann cones and unprojected LMI obstructions concern different embeddings or conclusions. A bounded priority comparison, with 84 queries and 25 primary PDF retrievals, found no full target predecessor in inspected bodies. Worldwide priority and current worldwide openness remain unestablished.

The deposit includes the proof, TeX source, scope and priority supplement, authored independent adversarial audits and portable exact symbolic arithmetic verification (Python 3.10 or later, standard library only). The three unchanged symbolic baselines verify the full coordinate, polynomial projector and mixed-minor identities. Forty-five defective-certificate executions test embedding coefficients and certificate structure or metadata; they reject before the latter identity checks. Finite checks do not replace the written proof or Fawzi's theorem. AI tools were used extensively in solving, verifying, source auditing and preparation. metadata.title: Forward generation does not ensure GNS descent: an explicit continuous counterexample
metadata.description: Generation by an observed algebra and its forward translates does not ensure descent through a general dilation's fixed expectation-GNS representation. This research note constructs a unital separable, injective, point-norm continuous C*-dilation of the two-state exponential relaxation semigroup, exactly forward-generated by C2. Its GNS image is M2, and an explicit nonzero positive kernel element leaves the kernel at every positive time. This refutes the concrete generation-only proposal in Skeide's 2009 module-approach problem. The clock/evaluation/cocycle mechanism is credited to Burgarth, Facchi and Hillier; the negative phenomenon is also a short unstated corollary of their earlier clock model. Finite-unitary and first-derivative antecedents are credited to Dive, Mintert and Burgarth and to vom Ende. No new general dilation method or literature-first priority is claimed. Stronger minimality conditions and extension after separately imposed kernel invariance remain outside the result. metadata.title: Generic Cantor actions of Z wr Z are hyperfinite
metadata.description:
We give an affirmative answer to Question 3 in Iyer's contribution, joint with Shinko, to Oberwolfach Report 2/2025, printed page 115. A dense G_delta in the space of all continuous actions of the restricted wreath product Z wr Z on Cantor space has hyperfinite orbit equivalence relation on the entire space. The auxiliary Borel theorem assumes an equivariant profinite shift height and permits stabilizers. Finite-width lamp slabs satisfy the compatible-metric theorem of Conley, Jackson, Marks, Seward and Tucker-Drob; the entire exceptional integer-height preimage has a separate finite Borel exhaustion.

The generic-height construction is an explicit specialization of established principles of Akin, Glasner and Weiss, Doucha, and Doucha, Melleray and Tsankov, all credited in the note. Iyer and Shinko's baseline is cited as a published 2025 paper. A dated, bounded priority audit found no exact earlier resolution in the inspected corpus. metadata.title: Maximal norm discontinuity for a bounded-region continuum fermion interaction
metadata.description:
We give a self-contained explicit counterexample for the existential unregularized bounded-region fermion question on printed page 371 of Oberwolfach Report 7/2025, with pointwise operator-norm topology distinguished from strong-operator topology on page 365. In dimension three, one fixed smooth nonnegative radial compactly supported pair potential and one fixed interaction ball give a fixed smooth normalized annihilation mode whose Heisenberg norm differences tend to the maximal value 2. Explicit packed finite-particle Slaters and times pi/(2N+1-kappa) witness the same vector-norm limit, a stronger vector asymptotic, and changing normal-state values tending to 4. Both diagonal-density and normal-ordered interactions are covered with ordered-pair coefficient 1 and no ultraviolet smearing. A fixed smooth-cutoff commutator, Slater second moment and two-sector Duhamel comparison give error O(N^(-1/6)+N^(-1/3)). The kinetic energy acts on all of R³. Continuity on every fixed vector and in every fixed normal state remains valid.

metadata.title: A rotational obstruction to prescribed-end Veech realization
metadata.description:

metadata.title: Intermediate-area cylinders in the principal quadratic stratum
metadata.description: We derive a Poisson limit for intermediate cylinder areas in the principal holomorphic quadratic stratum Q(1^(4g-4)), with the square-count cutoff tending to infinity before the genus. For every s_g tending to zero with g s_g tending to infinity, normalized cylinder areas divided by s_g converge to a Poisson point process of intensity dx/(2x). Compact-window counts converge jointly with every fixed joint moment. The count in Delecroix's original window [1/sqrt(g),2/sqrt(g)] tends to Poisson(log(2)/2), and its mean and variance tend to log(2)/2. The proof extracts a uniform Gamma/Dirichlet comparison from the published geometric formulas of Delecroix-Liu and Delecroix-Goujard-Zograf-Zorich, with the underlying intersection-number estimates credited to Aggarwal. metadata.title: Quantitative persistence in a fixed-city area equation
metadata.description:
For every fixed finite collection of at least two distinct interior sites in the unit square and every strictly positive initial probability vector, consider the hard weighted-Voronoi area equation z_i prime = A_i(z) - z_i, where city i maximizes z_i^alpha times distance to the power -beta. We give a quantitative all-coordinate persistence theorem when beta > 2 alpha: an explicit time-dependent lower bound, a positive bound for all time, and a positive limiting inferior bound independent of the starting state. An asymmetric three-city instance with alpha=2, beta=8 has every share between 1/4096 and 2047/2048 for all nonnegative time. metadata.title: A periodic counterexample to the diffuse allocation characterization
metadata.description:
An explicit periodic diffuse measure on R^2 has a rooted law invariant under every measurable, pointwise-covariant, measure-preserving allocation determined by its original observed state, but fails the full joint mass-stationarity identity. The measure consists of horizontal Lebesgue lines with alternating densities one and two. Covariance and a finite per-period mass equation cover all allocations, including noninjective maps. In the defining unit-square mass-resampling experiment, the heavy-root event has probability two thirds instead of zero. A constant accompanying random element suffices. This gives a negative answer to Thorisson's historical Problem 4.1 and Last-Thorisson's Problem 7.5 in their stated unrestricted scope.

The entire existential negative conclusion is an elementary consequence of Last-Thorisson (2009), Example 7.1, their Lebesgue-product mass-stationarity proposition already in arXiv:1405.7566v1 (2014), Section 8 Proposition 1, retained in the 2015 version, and the full allocation-transfer calculation displayed in the note. Last-Thorisson (2023), Section 8 and Remark 8.1, give the canonical diffuse parallel-line/invariant-direction balancing obstruction; Khezeli-Mellick (2025), final Remark 3.2, explicitly identifies the product/atomic-quotient balancing-allocation reduction. Those balancing-existence statements have a distinct scope from the self-preserving characterization. The periodic rational-weight model is an elementary worked illustration of these established mechanisms. No new-discovery, novelty, firstness, exhaustive-priority or worldwide-current-openness claim is made. The first explicit recognition of the combined corollary and priority of the exact periodic formula remain unestablished by bounded searches.

The example is singular, two-dimensional and has a continuous translation stabilizer. It supplies no counterexample for positive-density measures, one-dimensional diffuse measures, free actions, absence of invariant directions, independent stationary backgrounds, or invariance under all preserving Markov kernels. metadata.title: Global Hessian realizations of statistical manifolds

Every smooth Hausdorff second-countable statistical manifold of fixed finite dimension n at least 1, without boundary and with positive-definite metric, admits a proper global statistical embedding into an open subset of R^N with one smooth positive Hessian potential, where N=binomial(2n+4,3). Orthogonal projection of the standard flat connection and its metric dual induces the prescribed ordered pair of torsion-free dual connections. For a general mutually dual pair, both torsions vanishing is necessary and sufficient for realization by a torsion-free dually flat ambient manifold. Countable zero-dimensional inputs are treated separately. The ambient neighborhood may be nonconvex and incomplete; dual affine coordinates are local. No finite-probability-model, global-gradient-injectivity or optimal-dimension conclusion is asserted.

The construction answers the historical realization question in item1(a) of Furuhata, Matsuzoe and Urakawa, Open Problems in Affine Differential Geometry and Related Topics (1998), in the stated smooth positive boundaryless scope. A smooth fiberwise right inverse produces an exact global Lauritzen pair, including the prescribed cubic and connection signs. A normal-neighborhood extension and a nonuniform Schur-complement penalty give one positive Hessian potential on a neighborhood of the entire embedded manifold, without compactness or uniform geometric bounds.

metadata.title: An explicit rank-two entropy-minimizing Fano degeneration
metadata.description:
We give an explicit smooth Fano fivefold whose unique global Han–Li entropy-minimizing valuation has rational rank two and is therefore nondivisorial. Its canonical first central variety is singular, so this first degeneration is nontrivial. The example is the product of Miao–Wang's established quadric-blowup threefold with the first Hirzebruch surface. Exact moment equations specify the two positive weights. A universal resultant argument and the classical Hermite–Lindemann theorem prove that their ratio is irrational. The associated graded anticanonical ring, canonical weight normalization, weak product soliton equation, and application of the established global optimality criterion are made explicit.

The construction satisfies the request discussed by Blum in Oberwolfach Report 17/2022, pp. 888–889, without a dimension bound or a product exclusion. Major inputs are due to Miao–Wang, Wang–Zhu, Han–Li, and Blum–Liu–Xu–Zhuang. The threefold factor was already announced in Miao–Wang's January 2024 preprint. No novelty, historical firstness, exhaustive priority, or continued-openness certificate is claimed.

metadata.title: An effective criterion for prescribed block-code extensions
metadata.description:
For a specified onto block self-map f of a nonempty two-sided irreducible sofic shift T, this note gives a complete finite computable criterion for extending that same map into T from a containing shift of finite type. It answers the specified-map question in Boyle's Problem 16.3, including its mixing case. For any total completion F of the local rule, let L be the allowed finite-word language and B the regular two-sided ideal of input words whose finite output is forbidden. Extension is equivalent to locally testable separation of L from B. An irreducibility-based saturation proof converts the credited Place–van Rooijen–Zeitoun2014 Theorem4.2 bound into the single canonical test L(T[N]) intersect B empty, with N=max(2,ell,4(|M|+1)) for a common recognizing monoid M. Success gives F(T[N])=T; failure excludes all other radii, completions and containing alphabets.

metadata.title: Three anti-invariant classes on a nonintegrable four-manifold
metadata.description:
We construct smooth nonintegrable almost complex structures on the closed real four-manifold given by a genus-two curve times an elliptic curve, with at least three independent real closed anti-invariant de Rham classes. metadata.title: A projective-line quotient of the Rogalski–Sierra algebra
metadata.description:
For the exact six-relation presentation R(alpha,beta) printed in the 2010 Oberwolfach report and 2012 Rogalski–Sierra article, the linear ideal I=(x3-x1,x4-x2) is nonzero, homogeneous and completely prime, strictly below the augmentation ideal. The exact quotient is the projective-line twisted homogeneous coordinate ring B(P1,O(1),sigma), with sigma[s:t]=[s+beta*t:beta*s+t]. The unital graded surjection has Hilbert series(1-z)^(-2), positive-dimensional projective target and GK-dimension 2. This decisively refutes both literal printed assertions for all prescribed algebraically independent parameters: uniqueness of the nontrivial graded prime and absence of nontrivial maps to any THCR. No classification, embedding, common graded quotient ring or surface-dimensional image is claimed.

The self-contained presentation theorem holds over every field for arbitrary alpha and beta^2!=1. In characteristic two it concerns the displayed algebra; the journal's fractional parameter identification with its geometric noetherian family is used only in characteristic different from two. Singular beta=+/-1 is excluded and has linear zero divisors. Classical quantum/Jordan-plane, degree-reduction, graded-twist and THCR machinery is credited.

metadata.title: A two-tail obstruction to ambient conjugation in Dlab groups
metadata.description:
We give an affirmative answer to the corrected Kourovka Notebook Problem 21.149. The compact-support Dlab group with slopes in the powers of two has an order automorphism that cannot be implemented by conjugation after any embedding into any standard real Dlab group. The ambient slope group is unrestricted, the embedding need not preserve an order, and the conclusion includes the full and reflected extended-real families.

The proof uses perfectness to separate the supports of commuting local groups, least action components and finite-tuple transitivity to obtain one uniform orientation, and a normalizer with infinitely many bump components near both source endpoints. One of these tails forces a forbidden descending sequence of ambient support components. A solvable affine-germ quotient treats the real-line left endpoint. The paper credits Gong, Yang and Zeng, arXiv:2609.18630, for the prior six-family rank-one theorem and one-tail support obstruction. It also distinguishes the earlier formally verified non-inner formulation from the corrected ambient question.

metadata.title: Equal dilatations deep in the Johnson filtration: a convex-core proof
metadata.description:
For every fixed closed oriented surface of genus g at least 2 and every fixed finite Johnson depth k at least 3, we prove that pseudo-Anosov log-dilatation multiplicities in I_g(k), counted up to conjugacy in the full orientation-preserving mapping class group, are unbounded. metadata.title: Quadratic convergence of SOS-density bounds on convex bodies
metadata.description:
For every fixed compact convex body K in R^n with nonempty interior and every fixed real polynomial f, the normalized Lebesgue global sum-of-squares density hierarchy of degree at most 2r has error at most C(K,f)/r^2 for every integer r at least 1. A self-contained elementary proof gives an explicit constant and a single global square on the whole body. A quadratic Taylor upper proxy, homothetic sublevel growth, and a fixed power of an endpoint Dirichlet polynomial yield a normalized first-moment bound without a logarithmic loss. This proves the quadratic upper rate in the convex-body/Lebesgue regime of OWR-16633-006, with the probability-density unit-mass convention explicitly restored. The known interval linear example shows sharpness of the worst-case exponent; no positive matching lower rate for every objective is asserted.

metadata.title: A negative answer to Nevo's homology-sphere decomposition question
metadata.description:

metadata.title: Coarse endpoint concentration at every diverging scale for one-dimensional space-time random walks
metadata.description:
For a nearest-neighbor walk on the integers in any fixed independent identically distributed space-time environment whose right-step probabilities lie strictly between zero and one almost surely, we prove superpolynomial concentration of the coarse quenched endpoint law around its averaged law. The intervals may have any deterministic lengths tending to infinity and any deterministic alignments, with no lower growth rate or uniform ellipticity assumption. For every fixed positive discrepancy threshold and every inverse power of time, the corresponding environmental tail is bounded by that inverse power eventually. Constants depend on the fixed law and the eventual threshold may depend on the scale sequence. The theorem gives the affirmative one-dimensional assertion contrary to Conjecture 1 in Noam Berger's contribution to Oberwolfach Report 38/2009.

Novelty and historical priority remain unresolved. The bounded audit established no exact full anticipation, but could not access the complete original texts of Boldrighini-Minlos-Pellegrinotti (1999 and 2004), Boldrighini-Pellegrinotti (2001), or Berard (2004). Stronger estimates in those papers have not been eliminated as antecedents. We claim no firstness, independent discovery, new method, or present-day open status. Classical replica, martingale, coalescing and bounded-differences methods are credited, including late-layer and local-corrector precedents of Dunlap-Gu and Barraquand-Rychnovsky.

metadata.title: Semibrace existence on meet-semilattices: an attributed classification
metadata.description:
For the four semibrace identities printed in Dietzel's Problem 3, OWR9/2023, every nonempty meet-semilattice with any prescribed distinguished element admits a semibrace via right projection. A realization that is also an L-algebra exists exactly when the distinguished element is greatest; in every such realization the logical order equals the original meet order. Under the separately attested meet-monoid convention, both existence questions require a greatest element. The result concerns existence, not classification of all multiplications, self-similarity or additional cancellation axioms. It includes arbitrary infinite and nondistributive semilattices.

This note is attributed exposition and explicit verification of the full printed existence answer. The joint multiplication, greatest element when the first argument is below the second and their meet otherwise, is exactly Castiglioni-San Martin's 2016 operation (arXiv:1611.09589v1, p.7, Example3.5(4)); their bounded semilattice means greatest element only, with no bottom assumption. metadata.title: A designed tree model with a sharp congestion–fragmentation transition
metadata.description:
We give an analytically tractable designed-tree example motivated by Aldous's conceptual congestion toy-model request. For a bounded-degree binary physical tree with k leaves on each root side and k squared cross-root demand streams, strictly positive linear capacity prices uniquely give the cheapest fixed-topology enlargement carrying doubled unit demands. An exact transportation-cut formula and an all-cuts probability estimate confine the joint marginal-admission and spare-connectivity change to an interval of width 16 sqrt(log(k)/k) around mean doubled demand. In the two outer phases every optimizer respectively leaves the whole tree spare or saturates every edge. The window is an upper bound, not an exact critical scaling theorem.

metadata.title: A fixed birational map without a prime-field cycle-distribution limit
metadata.description:
For the fixed birational map L(u,v)=(u,(u²+1)v), every prime p congruent to 3 modulo 4 gives a permutation of the full affine plane F_p². With point-weighted periods normalized by p, the distribution function at every fixed 1/2≤x<1 equals 1−φ(p−1)/(p−1)+o(1), has limsup 1 and liminf at most 23/24. Neither these CDF values nor the period probability measures converge on any further admissible prime subset of positive upper relative density.

A separate proposition covers every odd prime on the invariant regular domain of size p(p-r), where r is zero or two. The primitive principal term is (p-r)φ(p−1)/(p−1). Under uniform-point deletion or arbitrary finite nonnegative assigned periods only on exceptional fibers, bounded statistics change by O(1/p). The regular CDF and a globally bounded continuous ramp thus exclude convergence on every positive-upper-prime-density selection under these conventions. Completed measures are on nonnegative reals; assigned periods may exceed p. Primes congruent to 1 modulo 4 still do not give full-affine permutations.

This is a precisely scoped application to the broad existence assertion in Vivaldi's 2004 Oberwolfach contribution, joint work with Roberts. The triangular family, quadratic primitive-value machinery, shifted-prime totient mean and continuous scalar empirical law are established and credited to the actual sources. The positive-density selection conclusion uses the old atomless scalar law, not merely the existence of two subsequences. No new map family, character-sum theorem, arithmetic mean, scalar law, universal elliptic theorem, polynomial-automorphism theorem or prime-average cycle theorem is claimed.

metadata.title: NP-completeness of the initial odd-ear prefix
metadata.description:
The variable-threshold decision problem beta(G)>=t for the maximum initial consecutive odd prefix of an open ear decomposition is NP-complete, even on finite simple 2-vertex-connected graphs with a universal vertex whose deletion leaves a connected bipartite graph. The initial circuit and one-edge ears are counted; the first even ear ends the prefix. This gives a full complexity answer to Sebo's OWR 2014 Question 4 and Benchetrit-Sebo's 2015 Question 3.3. It does not assert P!=NP, fixed-threshold hardness, closed-ear hardness or a theorem about the total number of odd ears.

The six-page note combines the classical factor-critical formulation with an explicit cone identity and a polynomial Set Cover reduction. Complete proofs include all preprocessing branches within the cone subclass, private-element perfect matchings, arbitrary partial blocks and omitted distinguished vertices, the exact loss identity d_i-k(a_i-b_i)=b_i(2k-a_i)>=0, connectivity forcing coverage, explicit polynomial encoding and NP certificates. The key estimate is k(r-s)<=T<k; whole-block optimality is never assumed. Classical structural and Set Cover results are credited as established inputs.

Actual primary sources were checked against alternative formulations: Sharifov's induced perfectly matchable objective permits disconnected selections, Weighted Connected Matching maximizes matching-edge weights rather than all induced edges, and constrained-ear and matroid-join results have different objectives. metadata.title: A singleton-supported cycle correction to Byrnes's differential-poset bound
metadata.description:
For every ordinary unweighted r-differential poset and n at least 2, an explicit nonnegative singleton-supported cycle rank q_n is subtracted from Byrnes's cumulative upper bound. The correction depends only on the two preceding incidence ranks. Terminal-preserving witness trees prove the cycle transfer b_n at least q_n. Standard reflected Young-prefix examples attain strict improvements from 31 to 30 for r=3 and from 20 to 19 for r=1, making coefficient one sharp. A singleton-successor sufficient condition, conditional two-witness equality characterization and the all-r rank-three consequence are proved.

This answers Majumder's printed request for an improvement of the Byrnes inequality in an incidence-dependent form. Stanley's general local recurrence, the separate combinatorial strict-growth-proof question and improvement of the global Fibonacci envelope are not claimed. Classical incidence identities, graph facts, singleton methods and Wagner reflection are credited. Gaetz-Venkataramana Proposition 3.4 already gives the exact rank-one two-singleton lemma used in the rank-three deduction; the witness poset families are standard. metadata.title: A sharp forest bound and an improved whisker bound for finite WARM graphs
metadata.description:
For power reinforcement on a finite simple undirected loopless graph, the infinitely reinforced edges almost surely form a forest for alpha > 4/3, for arbitrary positive vertex firing rates and arbitrary fixed positive integer initial counts. The known unit triangle obstruction shows that the strict forest constant cannot be decreased. For equal rates every surviving component is a tree of diameter at most three for alpha >= 17/4. The stochastic equality endpoint alpha = 4/3 and the suggested sharper whisker interval remain unresolved.

The deterministic contribution is an arbitrary-equilibrium weighted odd-cycle instability bound alpha > sec^2(pi/(2m)), robust under unequal rates, chords and attachments, together with exact scalar interval and unbounded-tail estimates for whiskers. Published finite stochastic convergence/support results, the even-cycle method, the uniform odd-cycle spectrum, triangle obstruction, and least-weight/champion arguments are explicitly credited. The earlier published proof already implies the weaker whisker bound alpha >= 24; the manuscript records a conservative strict version and its exact bridge. The forest result answers the finite forest-bound improvement requested by Kleptsyn in OWR12/2023 printed655 (30005455 / OWR-12697708-008).
